paras: The Fed Board majority and the regional Fed presidents (Powell, Cook, Barr, Jefferson, Waller, Bowman, Hammack, Logan, Kashkari) are an independent institution: they are the object of the Fed fight, and only Warsh also sits in a faction. The Guardrails Coalition on AI (Amodei, Warren, Schatz, Sanders) and the Democrats in the Russia coalition are external influencers. FTC Chair Ferguson (AI: “existing law first”, then a probe of three labs on Sep 30) has no single home.

What this cannot show. The grouping of people into eleven factions is my synthesis; the reports’ own placements are the evidence, and a different cut (for example merging Pentagon into Maximalists) is defensible. Footprint counts show where a faction has a dated position, not how much influence it has. Alliance edges mean parallel action; no document in the reports shows coordination except Vance’s public defense of Witkoff (Oct 21). Private deliberations are known only through anonymous sources in the reports. A “no dated position” cell neither agrees nor disagrees.
Where the reports conflict. I used the more recent or better-sourced version and did not reconcile the rest.
Sonderling is acting head of the Office of Government Ethics on the Cook committee in the Economy report and Labor secretary in the Immigration report. I left his title off.
Blanche is acting attorney general in Immigration but confirmed 50-49 on Aug 8 in Epstein and Midterms. I used attorney general.
Epstein names Zacharia as press secretary; Midterms and press reports say she was fired Oct 16.
Pulte is FHFA director in Economy and Midterms, acting DNI for under six weeks in Iran, and still called DNI in an Oct 16 Breitbart piece. I used FHFA director.
Musk’s 2026 giving: about $366M this cycle (Russia), $91M of $119M by AI executives (AI), $100-120M planned for America PAC with under $1M spent by Sep 3 (Midterms). Not reconciled.
The China truce ends Jan 10, 2027 in Tariffs; other reports say Nov 10.
Vance has no dated Venezuela position in that report, so he sits in the context row, not in a faction there.

What the motive lines rest on. The issue positions come from the ten reports. The motive lines come from a second round of outside reporting on the main players, listed below. Where that round found no personal stake, the bullet says so. Those lines are my reading; no source states anyone’s intent unless the bullet says so, and several people named deny any link (Kushner’s lawyer on Phoenix, the White House on World Liberty, Continental on Srpska, Homan’s case closed by DOJ). Players not researched in that round (for example Hegseth, Gabbard, Kent, Greene, Burgum, Gruters, Comer, Cooper and Caine) carry no personal-motive finding beyond what the reports say.
